title: What Is CTV Advertising? Streaming Ad Strategies | Simpli.fi

facts.fact: CTV stands for Connected TV, a television that connects to the internet and allows viewers to stream content.
facts.quote: CTV stands for Connected TV**, a television that connects to the internet and allows viewers to stream content.

facts.fact: The article defines CTV advertising as video ads delivered through streaming content on internet-connected TVs, including smart TVs and devices such as Roku, Fire TV, and gaming consoles.
facts.quote: delivers video ads through streaming content viewed on internet-connected television screens, including smart TVs and devices such as Roku, Fire TV, and gaming consoles.

facts.fact: Per the article, CTV ads may appear before, during, or after video content.
facts.quote: These CTV ads may appear before, during, or after video content and can be targeted based on household data, location, viewing behavior, and more.

facts.fact: Simpli.fi states that advertisers can access premium inventory across major streaming platforms via private marketplace deals.
facts.quote: Access premium inventory** across major streaming platforms via private marketplace deals.

facts.fact: Simpli.fi states that its AI-powered creative tools can turn social assets into CTV-ready video in minutes.
facts.quote: Use AI-powered creative tools** to turn social assets into CTV-ready video in minutes.

facts.fact: The article lists video completions, impressions, and offline conversions among the metrics CTV reporting can monitor in real time.
facts.quote: Monitor ad performance with metrics like completions, impressions, and offline conversions.

facts.fact: The article was published on January 13, 2026.
Simpli.fi states that advertisers can target CTV campaigns by household, ZIP code, or behavior using location-based filters.
facts.quote: Target by household, ZIP code, or behavior** with powerful location-based filters.
